dimension_literal_resolution.scan: linear over keyword/keyword.off + keyword/keyword.dat, take keyword/id.bin at matching row
dimension_literal_resolution.note: single matching row expected; first-match early exit

dimension_literal_resolution.scan: linear over dict entries to find matching dict_idx; this is the int16 code stored in country_code.bin
dimension_literal_resolution.output: us_code (int16, 1 for default; dict has ~215 entries)

build_phase.name: cn_us_bitset
build_phase.build: scan company_name/country_code.bin; for each r where cc[r]==us_code, set bit at company_name/id.bin[r]

join_order.probe: movie_keyword via aux CSR on keyword_id
join_order.notes: single keyword id → contiguous rowid range; yields candidate movie_ids (with dups)
for each mk movie_id v: row = title_pos[v]; if row>=0 and episode_nr[row] in [5,100), keep

join_order.probe: movie_companies via primary CSR on movie_id, semi-join on company_id in cn[us]
join_order.notes: first hit per movie is enough (EXISTS semantics for the conjunctive join)

join_order.build: cast_info via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.expected_rows_per_movie_avg: ~14 (36M/2.5M); 88 surviving movies × avg fan-out ≈ 1k-10k ci rows

join_order.notes: for MIN(an.name), iterate ALL aka_name rows in the range (cannot early-exit because a later row could be lex-smaller). Join an.person_id = n.id = ci.person_id collapses since aka_name and cast_info share person_id directly; the name table is only used as a connector and has no projected columns or filters, so it does not need to be probed (every ci.person_id corresponds to a valid name.id by FK).

data_structures.aggregation: two scalar running mins as std::string (one for an.name, one for t.title)

parallelism.strategy: morsel_driven over movie_keyword aux-CSR range for keyword=target
parallelism.reduction: per-thread local (min_name, min_title), final lex-min reduction across threads
parallelism.notes: Range is only 41,840 rowids — single-threaded would also work in <50ms on warm cache. Use parallelism for safety against cold cache (hdd) since random index probes can stall.

indexes.purpose: drive: select mk rows for target keyword (aux CSR)
map movie_id → title row to read episode_nr and title text
for each candidate movie, scan mc rows to test cn[us] semi-join
for each surviving movie, scan ci rows to obtain person_ids
for each person_id, scan aka_name rows for MIN(name)

hot_columns: movie_keyword/keyword_id.bin (sequential scan via aux CSR rowid order is random, but only 41,840 reads)
title/episode_nr.bin (random via title_pos; up to ~41,840 reads)
movie_companies/company_id.bin (sequential within CSR range per movie; small ranges)
cast_info/person_id.bin (sequential within CSR range per movie; up to ~10k reads total)
io_notes.advise: madvise MADV_RANDOM on title_pos and CSR offset/rowid arrays; MADV_SEQUENTIAL on column files within CSR scans (negligible benefit on hdd given small range sizes)

expected_runtime_class: milliseconds to low-seconds (88 surviving movies, ≤10k inner rows, varlen reads minimal)
